items.name: Moisture-wicking base layer
items.note: Synthetic or merino; cotton holds sweat and chills you when you stop.

items.name: Fleece or grid mid layer
items.note: Your working insulation for the climb itself.

items.name: Insulated (down or synthetic) jacket
items.note: Belay jacket for stops, camps and cold descents.

items.name: Waterproof shell jacket and trousers
items.note: Wind and precipitation protection; check taped seams.

items.name: Softshell or climbing trousers
items.note: Abrasion resistance for rock and snow.

items.name: Warm hat and neck gaiter
items.note: Most heat loss is from an uncovered head and neck.

items.name: Gloves plus spare liners
items.note: Thin liners for dexterity, thick gloves for summit cold.

items.name: Category 4 sunglasses and spare
items.note: Glacier glare causes snow blindness without high UV protection.

items.name: Climbing harness
items.note: Fits over your layers; check the belay loop and buckles.

items.name: Helmet
items.note: Protects against rockfall and falls on snow slopes.

items.name: Ice axe (or two for steeper ground)
items.note: Length and pick type depend on the route angle.

items.name: Crampons fitted to your boots
items.note: Test the fit at home; a loose crampon is a fall risk.

items.name: Climbing rope of suitable length
items.note: Length depends on pitch length and terrain.

items.name: Slings and cordelette
items.note: For anchors, extensions and improvised belays.

items.name: Locking and non-locking carabiners
items.note: A mix of sizes; inspect gates and screwlocks.

items.name: Belay or abseil device
items.note: Match the device to your rope diameter.

items.name: Ascender or prusik cord
items.note: For progress on fixed ropes and crevasse rescue.

items.name: Ice screws and snow pickets
items.note: Protection appropriate to ice and snow conditions.

items.name: Mountaineering boots
items.note: Stiff enough for crampons; check the sole flex and waterproofing.

items.name: Gaiters
items.note: Keep snow, scree and spindrift out of your boots.

items.name: Liner socks
items.note: A thin wicking layer reduces friction and blisters.

items.name: Thick wool or synthetic socks
items.note: Carry a spare pair; wet socks cause cold feet.

items.name: Camp booties
items.note: Warm feet in camp while boots dry.

items.name: Spare laces
items.note: A snapped lace high on a route is hard to improvise.

items.name: Paper map and compass
items.note: Still works when batteries and screens fail.

items.name: GPS device or route watch
items.note: Carry the route pre-loaded and know how to use it.

items.name: Satellite messenger or PLB
items.note: Mobile coverage is rare above the tree line.

items.name: Spare batteries for every device
items.note: Cold drains cells far faster than at home.

items.name: Power bank and cables
items.note: Keep it warm inside your jacket.

items.name: Two-way radios (if travelling as a team)
items.note: Agree channels and check-in times before leaving.

items.name: Route plan shared with someone at home
items.note: Include your objective, route and expected return time.

items.name: High-calorie snacks within reach
items.note: Eat before you are hungry; appetite drops with altitude.

items.name: Freeze-dried or cooked meals
items.note: Plan one more day of food than the itinerary requires.

items.name: Stove, fuel and windbreak
items.note: Check fuel quantity and that the stove lights cold.

items.name: Lighter and waterproof matches
items.note: Two independent ignition sources.

items.name: Insulated water bottle
items.note: An insulated bottle resists freezing overnight.

items.name: Water treatment (filter or tablets)
items.note: Melted snow still needs treating in many areas.

items.name: Electrolyte tablets or powder
items.note: Replace salts lost through heavy sweating.

items.name: Bowl, mug and spoon
items.note: Insulated mug keeps a hot drink drinkable.

items.name: First aid kit for the group size
items.note: Know what is inside it before you need it.

items.name: Blister kit
items.note: Tape, compeed-style dressings and scissors.

items.name: Personal medication
items.note: Carry your own supply; do not rely on the group kit.

items.name: Painkillers and anti-inflammatories
items.note: Check allergies and dosage with a pharmacist or doctor.

items.name: High-factor sun cream
items.note: UV rises sharply with altitude and snow reflection.

items.name: Lip balm with UV protection
items.note: Cracked lips are a small but constant distraction.

items.name: Emergency shelter or bivvy bag
items.note: For an unplanned night out or an injured partner.

items.name: Headlamp with spare batteries
items.note: Most rescues start with a descent in the dark.

items.name: Four-season tent with spares
items.note: Pole repair sleeve and a few spare pegs.

items.name: Sleeping bag rated below the expected minimum
items.note: Ratings assume a dry bag and a good mat.

items.name: Insulated sleeping pad
items.note: Ground cold, not air temperature, drains your heat.

items.name: Pillow or stuff sack
items.note: Small comfort that improves sleep at altitude.

items.name: Stuff sacks and pack liner
items.note: Keep the sleeping bag dry above all else.

items.name: Earplugs and eye mask
items.note: Shared tents and long daylight hours disrupt rest.

items.name: Pee bottle (winter camps)
items.note: Leaving the tent at night in deep cold is a real risk.

items.name: Climbing permit or park registration
items.note: Requirements differ by country and massif.

items.name: Insurance covering mountaineering and evacuation
items.note: Check the altitude limit and activity exclusions.

items.name: ID and copies (paper and photo)
items.note: Keep copies separate from the originals.

items.name: Cash in local currency
items.note: Card readers fail in remote valleys.

items.name: Printed itinerary and emergency contacts
items.note: Also leave a copy with someone at home.

items.name: Repair kit (tape, wire, multi-tool)
items.note: Fixes crampon straps, pole baskets and tent poles.

items.name: Waste bag (leave no trace)
items.note: Pack out what you pack in, including human waste where required.
